title: Small-Sensor Display Agreement
researchQuestion: How consistently do side-by-side consumer temperature and relative-humidity displays settle into the same displayed interval?
summary: The completed protocol examined a categorical method for comparing display stabilization and rounding behavior among ordinary consumer sensors placed together under routine indoor conditions. The public summary describes method and scope only and does not certify instruments or publish device-level findings.
eligibility: The closed protocol used ordinary consumer temperature and relative-humidity displays.
Displays remained side by side on a stable indoor surface for each observation interval.
Only displayed values and stabilization categories were within scope.
exclusions: The protocol excluded medical, industrial-control, safety-critical, and permanently installed building instruments.
No brands, serial numbers, purchase records, exact locations, photographs, or remote device connections were included.
participantActivities: Place selected consumer displays together on one stable indoor surface and allow an assigned settling interval.
Record displayed whole-unit or fixed-decimal values at scheduled points without adjusting the devices.
Classify agreement, rounding difference, and apparent stabilization using fixed response categories.

protocolSteps.title: Arrange
protocolSteps.description: Place the displays together on a stable surface away from direct heating or cooling.

protocolSteps.title: Settle
protocolSteps.description: Leave the arrangement unchanged for the assigned stabilization interval.

protocolSteps.title: Read
protocolSteps.description: Record displayed values in the same device order at each scheduled point.

protocolSteps.title: Classify
protocolSteps.description: Apply fixed agreement and rounding categories without assigning device accuracy.

dataRequested: Broad display category and available measurement channels.
Displayed values at assigned observation points.
Confirmation that the device arrangement remained unchanged.
dataNotRequested: Brand, model, serial number, purchase record, account, or network information.
Exact location, photographs, room identity, or information about occupants.
samplePrompts: Did each display remain unchanged during the final observation interval?
Do the displayed values occupy the same categorical agreement band?
Was the device arrangement disturbed after the settling interval began?
methodNotes: The method compared displayed agreement and stabilization behavior, not traceable measurement accuracy.
Device identity was replaced by a temporary observation label and was not part of the public method summary.
Fixed categories were selected before the comparison interval and applied in the same order.
limitations: Consumer displays can use different internal sensors, update intervals, rounding rules, and ventilation arrangements.
Side-by-side placement reduces some environmental variation but does not create a calibrated reference condition.
The protocol cannot support a product ranking, compliance claim, or accuracy certification.
publicSummary: The protocol established that an ordinary side-by-side comparison can be documented with fixed stabilization and agreement categories while avoiding unsupported accuracy claims. No device-level result, ranking, or certification is released through the public study page.
